title: Good app, extremely laggy on iPhone
body:
Been using Notion for years, I love the app, and though it takes some time to understand how it all works once you do it’s simple and fun to utilize. 

With that said the app is really really laggy on iPhone. 

A few issues I’ve found using Notion on iPhone:  

1. I cannot delete text on the app. Say I select text and press the x button to delete it on my iPhone keyboard, it will not delete. Even if I press x to delete it without selecting the text it won’t delete so I have to select and press the ‘cut’ selection.

2. Certain pages won’t load when I try to open them, it’ll display the loading icon for awhile and then seemingly crash and close the app.

3. Inserting photos and the page auto-scrolls downwards to the end of the page. Pretty self explanatory, but when I insert photos and then try to move them around the page it’ll start auto scrolling to the bottom of the page.

Review: The Ultimate "Brain" for AI Development
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Notion has completely transformed how I manage and execute technical projects. Instead of scattered notes, it serves as the ultimate external "brain" and central knowledge repository for my automated workflows, specifically when feeding context into Claude Code and my agentic systems.
What makes Notion indispensable for an AI-driven development environment:
 Structured Context: The ability to seamlessly organize markdown files (⁠.md⁠), system configurations, and project documentation makes it incredibly easy to pull structured data into an AI context.
 Clean Markdown Support: Because Notion handles markdown natively, exporting clean, structured data for programmatic use or CLI tools is seamless.
 Frictionless Organization: It provides a highly scannable, deeply organized hierarchy that keeps massive amounts of technical data manageable without feeling overwhelming.
Whether you are mapping out logic or building a dynamic knowledge base for AI agents to query, Notion bridges the gap between human planning and machine execution perfectly. Highly recommended for anyone running modern, agentic workflows.

As much as I hate AI, I really really loved Notion and I would have kept it if they’d have some option for toggling off the AI features. They’re just really obtrusive and obnoxious for how useless/harmful they are, like I don’t want an AI assistant helping me write and stealing my content. Previous review:
Just noticed that I, a paying Notion Plus subscriber can no longer use Notion AI.  Welp, I’m definitely not going to use Notion AI now that I have to upgrade and pay more than 4 times what I normally pay yearly.  And you can’t turn it off or even hide it!  Everyone knows AI is very flawed and yet these tech companies want to charge so much for it!  And anyone who uses Notion knows how flawed it is, which makes it all the more frustrating.  It’s got a truly great structure to it making it incredibly versatile, but it’s like a plane with small wings and no engines.  But hey, you can pay for a somewhat dim flight attendant.

OK, this is my previous review:

Just updated the app, sad to see image files load but then turn white and require me to scroll back up and then over the images to get them to show. Every time I load the page with images in it I have to scroll up and down again. My original review: it really needs a few things—most importantly, encryption for us poor folks. It looks like you have to be an enterprise customer to get anything resembling actual privacy and it’s unclear what you get is encryption. We live in a time where our data is making people tons of money. I’d rather they not make money off of my notes and my used habits. Also, this needs the same notes graph/map/diagram thingy that a few Notion competitors have that allows you to visualize how all of your notes are related to each other. It is such a cool and helpful way to see the big picture on your projects! The third thing I think it needs is just a slightly better UI. It does a lot but it can be pretty challenging to navigate/find everything. I haven’t checked yet but I suspect that YouTube is the user’s friend along these lines. Otherwise, Notion is a fricken Swiss Army Knife app—you can literally keep a journal, a journal within a journal, a wiki, multiple wikis, I can’t even list all the templates this thing has. However, the updated version compulsorily added three ugly and disturbing buttons at the bottom of each page: 1 of The search button (repeated function, which originally had shortcuts and the top search box); 2nd The AI button that occupies the most space (obviously not good for promoting its impractical AI functionality); Three New page button (the same repeats). title: AI might be good for some, but for me it was the end.
body:
Years ago, I was recommended this note tool via word of mouth. I initially loved it! Being able to switch between devices as I needed was a big plus for my writing, and I loved the stacking folders and clean ui. 

I had no need for ai when it launched. It was unobtrusive, however, so I carried on. Then, a badly implemented update caused a piece of writing I had worked on for hours to, with an easy keyboard stumble, be completely rewritten. Completely. Hours of work chewed up and spit out into slush. :/ I promptly closed the app and stopped writing in it.  

Years later, I have found a software I like better, with no intrusive ai and no cloud services, so my notes are no longer at risk in a server I don't have access to. I have zero faith that notion has kept anything I ever wrote secure. They continue to say one thing and do another. I am done. 

In logging in to transfer my notes, I notice that the program is buggy and slow in ways it never was years ago. Buffers like crazy. It's actually kind of heartbreaking to see how far this app has fallen.

There are better options out there, with more security and better customization. Even if you want ai in a notes app, there are more clean and helpful options that do not compromise your experience. Why pick notion? I never will again.

Notion is the greatest platform ever built. I don’t say this lightly or throw this around often. 

You can literally do anything you want in notion. If you’re a lightweight user it’s an aesthetically pleasing version of word with a better mobile experience and killer keyboard shortcuts.

If you’re a super user - there is no ceiling. You can run sprint boards for engineers, you can build board presentations, you can build a deal board for sales folks, you can leverage call recording and meetings notes. 

If you’re a small biz owner and don’t want to spend on software you can literally make pages shareable and have a website, run emails, have a calendar etc.

title: Intentional Lack of Important, Basic Features
body:
Probably the worst notes app I’ve ever had the pleasure of experiencing, all because they’ve done the work to be found near top search results through sponsored means, whether that be comments or ratings. 

It makes no sense why another individual would have to create an account just to see my document, especially if they’re already going to be defaulted to read-only mode. This ultimately makes this app incredibly difficult to work with when working with others, as the question, “Why didn’t I just make it in a text document with word or Google Docs?” There are plenty of open-source options. 

Don’t even get me TOO started on the fact that the app allows offline downloads, but clearly is so insecure in its desire to consume user data and user interactions that you, as the user, are not allowed to even OPEN THE APP when you’ve disabled “Use Cellular Data” in your phone’s settings. 

Actually pointless. I’ll unfortunately be moving all of my notes over to a smarter, more competitive app; wherein I don’t have to pay $20+ a month for automatic offline downloads, just to not be able to use the app if I turn cellular data off. Actually insane. Unlucky.

title: Powerful, flexible, and great for staying organized
body: Notion is one of the most versatile productivity apps I’ve used. It works well whether you’re managing personal notes, tracking projects, or collaborating with a team. The flexibility is its biggest strength—you can start simple and gradually build more complex systems as your needs grow. I especially like how everything lives in one place: documents, databases, tasks, and ideas are easy to connect and reorganize. The interface is clean and modern, and once you get used to it, workflows feel very natural. Syncing across devices is reliable, which makes it easy to switch between phone, tablet, and desktop without losing context. There is a learning curve at the beginning, but plenty of templates and community resources help you get started quickly. Overall, Notion is a powerful tool for anyone who wants more control over how they organize information and work. It’s not just a note-taking app—it’s a flexible workspace that adapts to how you think and work.

title: minimal appearance options. slight headache.
body:
i know that this critique seems minor, but it’s very cumbersome to use the app when the look of it gets in the way. 

for example, the ai chat bubble that persistently exists on every single window—every page and every database view—is not only unnecessary, it’s part of a larger problem: we can’t get rid of it. including more visibility options seems in line with the main pro of notion: flexibility. 

for how much flexibility one gets in the functional parts of notion—e.g., in the views, the keystrokes, and the properties—it’s strange that little effort is put into the flexibility of the interface. i’m sure y’all have had a lot of ideas for its interface bouncing around. why not include them all as options?

title: Ultimate flexibility. Some elbow grease requires.
body:
Notion in a word - flexible. 

Simplicity. Probably not. 

That’s not a criticism. That’s testament to how much you can do with it. 

A file manager is simple. Make some folders, store some files. Search them. Useful? Yes. Powerful? Not really. Flexible. No. 

It’s got a singular purpose. 

Notion is flexible and powerful. The trade off is knowing where to start. 

Notion can be a workflow tool. It can be a blog hosting platform. It can manage projects. Organise data for you and tag it. Be a research vault, holding articles, audio, imagery and video, all tailored and presented just the way you like it. Not a flat structure of files. No, think a rich webpage with links passing to other pages, embedded media. The works. 

And it’s not that hard to get any of it working. Notion does a lot to make this as easy as it can be. It’s all GUI driven. It’s impressive. 

Sure it has quirks. Could you get something this flexible to work without them? Probably not. 

You will struggle to find a product as feature rich. Its AI tooling isn’t just a gimmick either. It can truely help you manage and create content. 

Ask yourself - do you need this much in a tool? If you need a fantastic collaboration platform; a place to collect and organise your research project; a project management tool to help run your SMB; a way to effectively manage you local soccer club - notion could be your answer. 

If you just want somewhere to save your photos, or store some files, it’s overkill. 

Overall an excellent product in the right context.

The iOS 26 design update removed breadcrumbs (page navigation) from the top of a page and placed it under the more options menu.

Breadcrumbs are a core part of UX and aid in accessibility. 

They tell us where we are.

Add them back to the top of the page so users don’t have to click an extra two buttons just to see the breadcrumb list.

Additionally, the breadcrumb block on mobile is odd. If you add it to a page it just shows you the name of your current page until you tap on it. It should show the breadcrumb list; use "..." like you used to if you have to.

title: Outstanding
body:
Notion is an exceptional productivity app that excels in every aspect of modern digital workspace management.

Usability: Notion is remarkably intuitive, with a seamless drag‑and‑drop interface and flexible page structure that makes organizing notes, tasks, and databases effortless. Even new users can quickly navigate and build workflows without a steep learning curve.

Performance: The app runs smoothly across devices, with lightning‑fast syncing between desktop, mobile, and web. Pages load quickly, and even large databases or complex dashboards maintain consistent responsiveness.

Design: Its minimalist, clean, and elegant design enhances focus without distractions. Subtle typography, spacing, and colour options let users create aesthetically pleasing layouts while maintaining clarity.

Features: Notion offers a powerful all‑in‑one toolkit: collaborative workspaces, relational databases, kanban boards, calendars, wikis, AI assistance, and extensive templates. The flexibility to customise every page for personal or team needs makes it stand out.

Value: With its robust free plan and versatile paid options, Notion delivers exceptional value for individuals, students, and businesses alike. It replaces multiple apps, effectively reducing costs and streamlining workflows.

Overall, Notion sets the standard for productivity and organisation, offering a versatile and beautifully designed platform that empowers users to work smarter and more creatively.

title: Fix Some Features
body:
I got recommended Notion for documents and images. The good thing about Notion is that when viewing images, you can zoom in perfectly and the image is not compressed in any way. I used this feature for a good while, and I always found it useful.

But, recently, after the new updates, the process has gotten a little bit tedious when captioning images, as the three dots are no longer there at the top-right corner of the image so you can easily select the "Caption" option instead of holding on the image to do so. I really preferred the three-dots option. 

Also, when captioning an image, it causes the app to bug out, not allowing you scroll while editing the caption. This bug has frustrated me so much.

And lastly, when wanting to view an image directly, you used to be able to just tap on the image to view it. But, now you have to hold the image and press "View Original." That's just too cumbersome and tedious to keep doing over and over again. I want to be able to view images right away.

To summarize:
- The three-dots at the top right of each image was always very useful to quickly use other options such as captioning, but now its gone. I want it back.
- When captionning, does not allow you to scroll for some reason. This is very annoying.
- You cannot view images directly anymore, you need to hold to view. I want these features changed for a better experience on Notion.

This update was right outright awful, and I really hope you guys notice these problems and please fix them. Thank you for acknowledging, I sure hope you fixed these problems.

اعطيت التطبيق نجمة واحدة لكوني لم استطع استخدامه او تجربته! بسبب مشكلة اتجاه النص العربي (RTL) و بسبب عدم توفّر واجهة عربية (Arabic UI)، و في ادناه تحليل المشكلة و الحل الذي ينبغي على المطورين اعتماده.

- وصف المشكلة (Issue Description):
    
    يعاني المستخدمون العرب من قلب اتجاه السطر وتخبّط المحاذاة أثناء الكتابة بالعربية داخل نَوشَن (Notion). يظهر الخلل خصوصًا عند إدراج كلمات إنجليزية قصيرة داخل سطر عربي، مما يؤدي إلى اضطراب اتجاه النص وعدم اتساق العرض.
    
- خطوات إعادة الإنتاج (Steps to Reproduce):
    1. اكتب سطرًا عربيًا يبدأ بحرف عربي.
    2. أضف مصطلحًا إنجليزيًا بين قوسين بعد كلمة عربية مثل: اسمي احمد (ahmed) وأسكن بغداد (Baghdad).
    3. لاحظ تغيّر اتجاه السطر أو اختلاط المحاذاة يمينًا ويسارًا، خاصة عند نسخ السطر أو تعديله.
- النتيجة الحالية (Actual Result):
    
    اختلال اتجاه السطر وتخبّط المحاذاة، مما يصعّب القراءة والكتابة ويشوّه التنسيق.
    
- النتيجة المتوقعة (Expected Result):
    
    ثبات اتجاه النص العربي من اليمين إلى اليسار (RTL) حتى مع وجود مصطلحات إنجليزية قصيرة ضمن السطر، مع محاذاة مستقرة وموثوقة.
    
- الأثر (Impact):
    
    تجربة الكتابة للمستخدم العربي تتأثر سلبًا، ويصعب استخدام نَوشَن (Notion) لإدارة المحتوى اليومي أو الاحترافي. هذا يسبب إحباطًا ويجبر البعض على التوقف عن استخدام التطبيق.
    
- البيئة (Environment):
    
    لغة الكتابة العربية (Arabic). المشكلة تظهر في الويب (Web) وتطبيق الهاتف (Mobile App) على حد سواء بحسب ملاحظات المستخدمين.
    
- أمثلة سطرية (Examples):
    - اسمي احمد (ahmed) وأسكن بغداد (Baghdad)
    - سكربت الحلقة (Script) والعناصر الأساسية (Key Points)
- طلب التحسين (Request):
    1. دعم كامل لاتجاه النص العربي من اليمين إلى اليسار (RTL) داخل المحرّر.
    2. إضافة خيار لغة عربية للواجهة (Arabic UI) ضمن الإعدادات (Settings).
    3. تحسين التعامل مع المصطلحات الإنجليزية القصيرة داخل السطور العربية دون إفساد الاتجاه.
- ملاحظات إضافية (Additional Notes):
    
    يفضّل توفير إعداد لإجبار اتجاه الفقرة عربيًا عند الحاجة، وخيار تنسيق سريع يضمن عدم قلب الاتجاه حتى مع الرموز والروابط.

title: I’m glad I can use notion on iPad, but man…
body: I use this for simple writing, google docs level stuff, and this app has a lot off issues. I’m using the official iPad keyboard, and it’s absolutely awful with clicking. It’s hard to explain, but I feel I have to stop moving and click HARD every time I want to to start typing. And now since the new update, it just straight up doesn’t work. I click, the type line appears, then it unselects itself. I have to click several times, eventually it works. That’s awful. Fix that please. Another issue, the little taskbar is awful on iPad, I can’t move it around or out of the way with a swipe, I have no idea how to change the colour of text effectively since when I open that menu it’s hell to go back. There’s more, and after using this app for a year I can probably raise a lot more issues and I reckon they’d be fixed - Notion seems like a great company and they’ve made a fantastic product. But it almost seems like these issues have gone unnoticed? Perhaps low on priority? … if you can sort these sooner rather than later, that’d be very appreciated. Thanks for your time.
